analysis: Examined base text of EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (lines 1-991) and the complete patch. The only change (head lines 249-250) adds a `stopStringScope: stopStringScope` argument to EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request. The argument is a bridge-level property, not request-derived input visible here. It sits beside cacheScope/cacheEnabled, which feed cacheSalt (T-041 scoping). No admission, deadline, KV reservation, prefix-cache receipt, staging, or release path is altered in this file. Cache scope handling (cacheScope -> cbv2Request, checkpointScope at base line 253, SSD stage calls at 401-437) is unchanged. The semantics of stopStringScope are outside the supplied evidence, including whether it is folded into checkpointCacheSalt or the prefix chain hash, and how stop strings are matched and redacted on output. Integration should verify in EngineV2Translation and the bridge property definition that: (1) stopStringScope cannot widen or collide cache scopes across accounts (T-041, SEC-035); (2) it is not attacker-controlled in a way that affects cacheSalt; and (3) stop-string scoping cannot cause output to leak past stops or fail to terminate, which would be an availability concern (T-010-adjacent). No regression is identified from the visible change.
